evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% in methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), patient with eczema, possible workplace exposure

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% in petrolatum, 278 eczema patients, multicenter study
evidence.support_text: In a North American multicenter study (1979-1980), 1% of 278 patients patch tested with 1% methyl heptine carbonate in petrolatum reacted. The table row for reference 41 lists 3 patients reacting (score not given) at 1% in petrolatum, with irritancy not excluded.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% petrolatum, read at D3

evidence.experimental_conditions: 104 eczema patients with prior positive reaction to Peru balsam; 5% cinnamyl alcohol in petrolatum; 48 h closed patch test with Lysaplast Special patch (linen on cellophane disc, adhesive tape); applied to anterior/lateral thigh; patches removed after 48 h; reactions read 10–20 min after removal and again 72 or 96 h after removal; in 50% of patients, additional reading at 7–8 days (Hjorth, 1961a,b,c).
evidence.support_text: In a study of 104 eczema patients who had previously reacted to Peru balsam, patch testing with 5% cinnamyl alcohol in petrolatum using a Lysaplast Special patch (48 h occlusion on the thigh) resulted in 26 positive reactions. Readings were taken at 10–20 min after removal, again at 72 or 96 h, and in half the patients after 7–8 days.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% aqueous PG, patch test on eczema patients
evidence.support_text: In provocative tests, allergic reactions were observed in 2 of 880 (0.2%) eczema patients patch-tested with 2% aqueous PG.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% ascaridole (w/w in unknown vehicle), patch test on human patients with eczema; readings on D3 and D7
evidence.support_text: Three hundred and nineteen patients with eczema were patch tested with ascaridole 1%, 2%, and 5%. With increasing ascaridole test concentration, the frequency of positive reactions increased: ascaridole 1%, 1.4%; ascaridole 2%, 5.5%; and ascaridole 5%, 7.2%. The authors conclude that the study supports ascaridole being a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum; 441 eczema patients
evidence.support_text: Positive reactions to 2% cinnamaldehyde in petrolatum were observed in 5.4% of 441 eczema patients tested by the NACDG from 1977 to 1978.
